The DLKP cell line and its Adr resistant subpopulations (DLKP-A2B, DLKP-A, DLKP-A5F and DLKP-A10) were investigated to identify differentially expressed proteomes.
DLKP-A was obtained by continuous exposure of DLKP cells to high levels of Adr
DLKP-A cells were further exposed to increasing concentrations of Adr, and the selected subpopulation was established as DLKP-A10.

DLKP-A was established by continuous exposure of the DLKP cells (pDLKP) to escalating concentrations of Adr (Step 1: 0.05 µg/mL–0.8 µg/mL Adr for 11 months, Step 2: 0.8 µg/mL–1.75 µg/mL for 3 months and Step 3: 1.75 µg/mL–2.1 µg/mL for 3 months).
The DLKP-A10 variant was established via exposure of DLKP-A cells to increasing concentrations of Adr to a final concentration of 17.25 µM.
